p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--EVE: Every normative statement in this project's spec tree is **addressable**: it lives under a stable `{#kebab-anchor}` and is cited by URI, never by paraphrase.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--COR: When the human corrects the agent, the correction cites the violated anchor: "you are violating `spec://…#verification.timeout` — the spec says 600 s, you wrote 300 s".

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--RES: Resolve the URI, read the unit, compare, fix.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--twe: Twenty tokens, exact hit — no guessing what "verification" means or which part is "wrong".

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--THE: The same contract binds the agent: when citing the spec — in chat, commit bodies, code markers, review notes — cite the anchor, never a paraphrase and never a line number.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--EAC: Each fact has exactly one authoritative anchor.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--NEV: Never copy a normative value into a second file — cite the anchor instead.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--two: Two copies *will* diverge, and a later session cannot tell which one binds.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--CRI: Critical constraints live at the START or END of a file, never buried mid-document.

p.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--mod: Models attend to the edges of context ("Lost in the Middle", Liu et al. 2023/2024); a mid-file invariant is an invariant the reader statistically skipped.

facts.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--POI: PROP vs FEAT, what goes where, the `.human/` buffer: @spec://org.vibevm.world/addressable-specs/flows/addressable-specs/spec-tree-layout#root

facts.org-vibevm-world--addressable-specs--NEV: Never cite a spec section by paraphrase when an anchor exists.
Never duplicate a normative value into a second file — cite its anchor.
Never bury an invariant in the middle of a file.
Never rename or delete an anchor that has ever been cited — anchors are immutable; retire with a tombstone instead.
Never invent an anchor — resolve the URI and read the unit before acting on it.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--LARGE-: This project executes large changes as **campaigns**: multi-commit work planned in a written campaign plan, executed as gated phases, resumable cold by any session.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--PROPOS: When the owner commissions work that spans **more than one session or more than a handful of commits**, propose a campaign plan before touching the tree.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--the-pl: The plan is one document carrying five roles:

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--write-: Write the plan so a fresh session — or a different person — executes it with no memory of the planning conversation:

facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--COLD-M: the owner's mandate quoted verbatim and dated,
facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--COLD-B: baseline and exit state as exact counts,
facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--COLD-F: current-state facts verified at writing time,
facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--COLD-D: decisions with their rejected options and reasons,
facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--COLD-A: and a runnable whole-campaign acceptance script.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--WRONG-: Wrong current-state facts are the most expensive class of plan bug — verify while writing.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--PHASE-: Phase 0 is spikes and probes — no commits — and it gates everything after.

p.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--EVERY-: Every later phase ends with the project's full gate panel green, and any phase boundary is a safe stop; the plan plus its execution ledger are the resume pointer.

facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--BOUNDA: Run the full gate panel; the floor must be green.
Write the phase's commit-map entry in the execution ledger — hashes, subjects, what each commit confirmed or falsified.
Refresh the plan's status line ("Phase N landed, floor green, next: Phase N+1").
Escalate anything only the owner can decide as a review point: OPEN, then RESOLVED with the ruling verbatim.

facts.org-vibevm-world--campaign-plans--NEVER-: Never start Phase 1 while a Phase 0 spike is red — a red spike rewrites the affected Decision first, in the plan, in place.
Never commit during Phase 0. Spikes leave findings, not tree changes.
Never do discovered work silently "while I was here" — it enters the phase and the ledger explicitly, or it is deferred by name.
Never close a campaign without the report checking every prediction — a campaign that skips the report learns nothing durable.
Never carry a deferral outside the plan file — the deferrals ledger is where deferrals live, and the next campaign's mandate drains from it.

p.org-vibevm-world--comparative-research--: This project has a genre for studying external systems — a competitor, a predecessor, an adjacent tool.

A **comparative research document** is a self-contained, evergreen study: readable months after publication without the original sources, structured as a two-way gap analysis, closing with numbered roadmap deltas.

When the user asks to study, evaluate, or compare against an external system — "what does X actually do?", "should we copy X's feature?", "audit that space before we build" — start from the skeleton in @spec://org.vibevm.world/comparative-research/flows/comparative-research/research-template#root and hold the laws:

facts.org-vibevm-world--comparative-research--: **Quote first, critique second.** The subject speaks in its own words — fenced verbatim quotes with access dates — before any judgement is written.
**Two-way gaps.** One section for where we trail, one for where we lead, argued with equal rigor.

**Deltas, not decrees.** Actionable findings become numbered proposals, each with a priority and a target home in the spec tree. The study never ratifies its own proposals; acceptance happens downstream, per @spec://org.vibevm.world/comparative-research/flows/comparative-research/from-research-to-roadmap#root.
**Re-fetch list.** Every source URL with access date, plus the subject's version at capture, so the study can be refreshed instead of rewritten.
Never paraphrase where a dated verbatim quote can stand — the quote survives link rot; the paraphrase decays into rumor.
Never write a one-directional gap analysis — trail-only is marketing for the subject, lead-only is marketing for us.
Never ratify a delta inside the research doc — it proposes; acceptance is recorded downstream.
Never let a study silently outlive its subject's next major release — stale-flag it and refresh via the re-fetch list.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--PRO: This project runs **two writers over one file set** — a human and a coding agent both edit the spec tree, the tests, and the code.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--CON: They *will* write contradictory things; that is normal cooperation, not an error.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--WHA: What is forbidden is resolving a contradiction silently.

org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--hie.title: The hierarchy

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--EVE: Every disagreement between layers is settled by fixed priority:

org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--hie.fence: Human > Spec > Tests > Code > volatile state

facts.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--HUM: The human may change the spec; nobody else may — silently.
facts.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--COD: Code must conform to the spec, never the other way around.
facts.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--TES: Tests are the spec in executable form: a test that contradicts the spec is a bug in exactly one of the two, never both.
facts.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--THE: The volatile state file is a record, dead last: when it disagrees with anything above it, it is stale.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--IF-: If you believe the spec is wrong: **implement the spec anyway**, add a marker at the point of disagreement —

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--SUR: — and surface it in the end-of-session report.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--THE: The human decides in the next cycle.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--thr: Three lines of text; seconds to write; a minute to read.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--CLI: Re-read the relevant spec section → re-read the relevant reference chapter → check the closest analog in the project → if still unclear, pick the conservative interpretation (the one cheapest to reverse), mark it with a REVIEW, proceed, and flag it in the report.

facts.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--NEV: Never silently modify a normative spec value.
Never resolve a spec-vs-code disagreement by assuming the code is newer. Recency is not authority; the hierarchy is.
Never remove someone else's REVIEW marker without resolving it.
Never invent semantics when the spec is silent — mark the choice and proceed conservatively.

p.org-vibevm-world--conflict-protocol--rec: Recovery drills for when the protocol has already been broken: @spec://org.vibevm.world/conflict-protocol/flows/conflict-protocol/failure-modes#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--FACT: A fact ("timeout is 600 s") is recoverable from the code in a second.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--REAS: The reason it is 600 s cannot be recovered at all — unless it was written down when the decision was made.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--ANY-: Any choice a future reader could plausibly re-open — a library pick, a constant with consequences, a protocol shape, a rejected approach — gets a **four-field record at the spec anchor that governs the value**:

td.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--ROW-: The chosen value or approach. One line.
Concrete and cited: a measurement, a constraint, an incident — with data.
One line per alternative, each carrying its rejection reason.
A measurable trigger: metric + threshold + where it is observed.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--NO-S: There is no separate ADR directory and no immutable numbered log.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--GOVE: The spec section that governs the value IS the record; evolution is an edit plus a changelog line; history lives in git.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--in-s: When the user makes a decision during a session:

facts.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--PROP: Propose recording it at the governing anchor, with all four fields, **before the session ends** — an unrecorded decision does not survive the session boundary.
facts.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--ASK-: If the why or the trigger is not known, ask. Do not invent data; do not record a two-field stub.
facts.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--READ: Before changing any value governed by a record, read the record. Re-open it only by naming its trigger state ("the trigger fired: …" / "the trigger has not fired, but …").

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--trig: Trigger design and the periodic sweep: @spec://org.vibevm.world/decision-records/flows/decision-records/revisit-triggers#root.

org-vibevm-world--decision-records--why.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--AGEN: The agent cannot ask Vasya why the library was chosen.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--re-d: It re-derives from what it can read, and the code shows the value, not the constraint — so it re-litigates: "600 s looks arbitrary, propose 300 s for performance."

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--RECO: A recorded decision is immunity from re-litigation.

p.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--TRIG: A recorded trigger is what keeps the immunity from hardening into dogma.

facts.org-vibevm-world--decision-records--NEVE: Never write "because it is better" — a why cites a measurement, a constraint, or an incident, or it is not a why.
Never re-litigate a recorded decision without naming its trigger state first.
Never put a decision's why into a commit message only. The commit cites the record; the spec carries it.
Never record a decision with a missing reason or a missing revisit trigger — that is a fact with decoration, not a record.

p.org-vibevm-world--dev-runtime-docs--SETU: A project's setup and runtime documentation is **load-bearing** — it is the file someone reaches for when the build breaks, the environment is wrong, or a prerequisite is missing.

p.org-vibevm-world--dev-runtime-docs--EVER: Every change that touches the **toolchain, prerequisites, environment variables, paths, or bootstrap steps** updates the relevant setup/runtime doc **in the same commit**.

p.org-vibevm-world--dev-runtime-docs--NEVE: Never ship a setup change with the doc update deferred — deferral is exactly where the drift these files exist to prevent lives.

facts.org-vibevm-world--dev-runtime-docs--NEVE: Never ship a dev-env or runtime-setup change with its doc update in a later commit.
Never let the setup docs describe a toolchain the project no longer uses.

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--PROJ: This project ships the **DISCOVERY collaborative-research prompt**, a distributable user-level prompt that reshapes an LLM session into structured co-inquiry.

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--ARTI: The artifact lives at @spec://org.vibevm.world/discovery-prompt/flows/discovery-prompt/DISCOVERY-PROMPT (the whole-document address: the payload is a title-less prompt, so it carries no `#root` anchor to cite).
It is a **payload for a fresh session**, not standing instructions — do not load it into context outside an explicit deployment request.

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--REAC: When the user asks for a research, discovery, or exploration session — comparing designs, mapping an unknown problem space, stress-testing a hypothesis — reach for the artifact: fill its `<VARIABLES>` block and paste the whole text as the first message of a fresh conversation.

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--depl: Deployment steps and a piece-by-piece walkthrough: @spec://org.vibevm.world/discovery-prompt/flows/discovery-prompt/usage#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--DEPL: Once deployed, the prompt replaces the default helpful-assistant frame with a response grammar (PrimaryHypothesis carrying an explicit 0.0–1.0 confidence, AlternativeInterpretations, MetaReflection), a mandatory adversarial self-objection before any answer is finalized, and hashtag intensity knobs (`#hot`, `#cold`, `#reboil`, `#superthink`).

p.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--STAN: Its stance in one line: uncertainty is data, not failure.

facts.org-vibevm-world--discovery-prompt--NEVE: Never mix the discovery grammar into a coding session uninvited — its overhead pays off only when the answer space is genuinely open.
Never edit the artifact in place; adapt a copy via the re-derive prompt in @spec://org.vibevm.world/discovery-prompt/flows/discovery-prompt/usage#re-derive.
Never treat the confidence numbers as guarantees — they are calibration aids, not measurements.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--TH: This project uses the **atomic commits** discipline as its Git contract.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--ON: One commit carries exactly one idea, and the commit message explains *why*.
**One commit = one logical change**, not one file changed.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--A-: A session that produces (a) a typo fix, (b) a refactor, and (c) a schema update is **three** commits, not one.
A feature that touches fifteen files for one coherent reason is **one** commit, not fifteen.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--CO: Commit messages follow the **git-conventional-commits** flow — a sibling package: `spec://org.vibevm.world/git-conventional-commits/flows/conventional-commits/conventional-commits#root`.
Conventional Commits is the *format*; this flow is the *atomicity* (one commit, one idea).

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--TH: The two are distinct and run together — a `feat: add foo, bar, baz` message is valid Conventional Commits and a violation of the atomic rule.

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--ST: Run `git status` and `git diff HEAD`. Name every change by intent.
Group changes into atomic commits — one commit per intent, not per file.
Stage and commit each group separately with a well-formed message.
Do not amend or force-push commits that are already pushed; create a new commit instead, unless the human explicitly approves history rewriting.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--sp: Procedure for splitting a messy working tree: @spec://org.vibevm.world/git-atomic-commits/flows/atomic-commits/splitting-large-changes#root.

org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--wh.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--WH: **Diff as verification.** Humans verify code by reading diffs. A diff that mixes three concerns is not verifiable in one pass.
**Rollback precision.** `git revert <sha>` must undo the wrong thing without also undoing two correct things.
**Commit log as decision record.** The message is the only place where *why* survives after volatile session notes and spec prose decay.

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-atomic-commits--NE: Never mix refactor + feature + docs + bugfix in one commit.
Never write a subject that summarises *what* changed — the diff does that. Write *why*.
Never `git commit --amend` on a pushed commit without explicit human approval. Same for `git push --force`.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-attribution-policy: This project keeps its repository **human-authored on every surface**.

This is the project's chosen default posture; the alternative (open disclosure) is documented in this flow's @spec://org.vibevm.world/git-attribution-policy/flows/attribution-policy/disclosure-alternative#root and a project may adopt it instead by editing this snippet.

Never attribute authorship of any part of this repository to an artificial-intelligence or neural-network–based system of any kind — no commit messages, no Git trailers (`Co-Authored-By`, `Signed-off-by: <model-name>`, or similar), no branch or worktree names, no code comments, no README lines, no release notes, no CI metadata.
This applies to every such system regardless of provider, model family, or whether it runs locally or in a cloud.
Some jurisdictions regulate or may come to regulate machine authorship of software.
This project is not currently subject to such regulation and violates no present law; the owner chooses the posture proactively, so that any future regulation finds no hook in this repository.
The surface this repository presents is: a human wrote this code, full stop.

This is a *publication posture chosen by the repository's owner*, not a deception of any party entitled to the information: the agent executing it is told the real reason (this section), and the policy itself is recorded openly here.

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-attribution-policy: This snippet and `spec/flows/attribution-policy/` are the **only** places in the project where AI tooling is discussed in the attribution sense. Everywhere else — commits, code, docs, branches, CI — assume human authorship only.
**Product scope is carved out.** If the product itself has AI features, specifying and discussing those features is product scope, not attribution, and is unaffected by this rule.

**Technical AI-workflow documents remain legal and unchanged** — checkpoint-file procedures, session protocols, agent instructions. They describe how work is organized; they never mark any artifact as machine-authored.
Never add a trailer or signature naming a model or an AI product to any commit.
Never mention model, agent, or AI-tool names in commit messages, branch names, or code comments.
Never state or imply machine authorship in any repository artifact.
Never weaken, widen, or restate this policy anywhere else in the repository — one policy, one place. Changing it is one edit to this file, made by the owner.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--THE-DEFA: The default posture for how much an agent decides on its own versus stops to ask, on the **commit and push** surface.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--ROUTINE-: Routine large changes proceed and are committed/pushed **without** a confirmation handshake:

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--ROUTINE-: touching many files for one coherent reason.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--the-appr: The approval was given upstream, when the work was authorised; a mid-work "shall I proceed?" is overhead already paid for.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--ASK-FIRS: Ask first for anything whose reversal costs work:

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-autonomy--RED-LINE: rewriting published history (rebase of pushed commits, `git commit --amend` on pushed work);
changing CI, signing, or secrets configuration;
**any operation whose reversal would cost work.**

p.org-vibevm-world--git-conventional-commi: Every commit message follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification: a **typed header** and a body that explains *why*.

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-conventional-commi: Subject **≤ 60 characters** (hard limit 72), imperative mood, lowercase after the prefix.
`scope` names the **narrowest accurate** subsystem (a crate, package, module, or area).

p.org-vibevm-world--git-conventional-commi: A blank line after the subject, then a free-form body that answers *why*, not *what* — the diff already shows what changed.

facts.org-vibevm-world--git-conventional-commi: Never write a subject that summarises *what* changed — write *why*.
Never capitalise the first word after the `type(scope):` prefix, and never omit the type.

p.org-vibevm-world--git-conventional-commi: Conventional Commits is the message **format**; it does not by itself enforce **atomicity** (one commit = one logical idea).
A `feat: add foo, bar, and baz` message is valid Conventional Commits *and* a violation of the atomic rule.
Atomicity is the separate `git-atomic-commits` flow; the two run together.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--PROJECT-: This project runs a **periodic health audit**: a recurring, judgment-heavy sweep over everything the per-commit gate cannot see, recorded as an append-only trend in `AUDIT.md`.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--THE-GATE: **The gate is the floor; the audit is what the gate cannot see.**
Where the gate answers *"did this commit regress covered code?"*, the audit answers *"what is wrong, rotting, or drifting that no commit will ever flag?"*.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--AUDIT-IS: The audit is **owner-triggered**, with a floor of **at least once per milestone** — run as part of, or right after, a milestone close-out.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--A-MILEST: A milestone is never declared done on an un-audited base.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--OWNER-RE: The owner re-runs it at will between milestones; no calendar cron is fixed.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--ONE-DATE: One dated section in `AUDIT.md` per run, each finding carrying an ID, its category, a one-line locator, a severity (P1/P2/P3), and a disposition (fixed/filed/accepted/open).

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--AUDIT-MD: `AUDIT.md` is committed to git — its history *is* the project's health trend.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--UNRESOLV: Unresolved findings carry forward to the next run and get re-judged.

p.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--USE-THE-: Use the **`health-audit`** skill: it reads the category checklist, walks it against the repository, and drafts the `AUDIT.md` section for your approval.

facts.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--NEVER-DE: Never declare a milestone done on an un-audited base — the audit is part of the close-out, not an optional extra.
facts.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--NEVER-LE: Never let a finding vanish without a disposition. Every finding is fixed, filed, accepted, or open — silence is not an option.
facts.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--NEVER-KE: Never keep findings only in the volatile session checkpoint files. The durable home is `AUDIT.md`; a checkpoint is reconciled *against* it, never a substitute for it.
facts.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--NEVER-LE: Never let the checklist fossilize. A new defect class a run discovers becomes a permanent category, so the same gap is never re-missed.
facts.org-vibevm-world--health-audit--NEVER-MI: Never mistake a green gate for a healthy project. The gate is blind by construction to uncovered code, out-of-gate trees, drift, and slow debt — each individually invisible, collectively corrosive.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--THE-PROJECT: This project has a **deliberate licensing posture**, decided once and recorded, not inherited from whatever a scaffold dropped in.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--two-things-: Two things are always true and must not drift:

facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--ONE-STATED-: The product ships under one stated licence (a `LICENSE.md` at the repository root; every sub-package states the same in its manifest).
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--EVERY-DEPEN: Every third-party dependency stays **permissive-only** — MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / Unlicense / equivalent. Strong copyleft (GPL / AGPL / LGPL) is forbidden by default; weak copyleft (MPL-2.0) is case-by-case.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--a-dependenc: A dependency's licence mingles with the product's.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--A-STRICTER-: A proprietary or source-available product that links a copyleft library can be forced to relicense — so the stricter the product's own licence, the *more* important the permissive-only rule, not less.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--REJECT-A-CO: Reject a copyleft dependency on licence grounds regardless of how good it is.

facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--WHEN-ADDING: Adding a dependency: check its licence before adopting it. A non-permissive licence is a hard no by default; surface it.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--WHEN-CHANGI: Changing the product's licence, or any bulk relicensing: this is an **owner decision** and an irreversible-threshold operation — never do it autonomously.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--WHEN-A-CHAN: A change touching the licence file, the manifest `license` field, or the third-party carve-out updates all of them together, in one commit.

p.org-vibevm-world--licensing--THE-DRAFT-E: The `draft-eula` skill drafts or reviews the posture.

facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--NEVER-ADD-A: Never add a GPL / AGPL / LGPL dependency by default — surface it as an owner decision.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--NEVER-RELIC: Never relicense the product, or any part of it, without the owner's explicit instruction.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--NEVER-LET-T: Never let the manifest `license` field and the `LICENSE.md` disagree.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--NEVER-REJEC: Never reject a dependency for being "too heavy" — weight is not a licence problem; licence is.
facts.org-vibevm-world--licensing--NEVER-CLAIM: Never claim a licence is permissive without checking; when unsure, treat it as non-permissive and ask.

spec.title: Flow: Managed Blocks

p.org-vibevm-world--managed-blocks--PROJEC: This project ships the **managed blocks** practice — a discipline for tool authors: how a tool writes into a file it does not own (an agent-instruction file, a shell rc, an ssh config, a shared project config) without destroying what the other tenants wrote.

p.org-vibevm-world--managed-blocks--the-la: The law fits on one line:

spec.fence: Own exactly one delimited block; never touch a byte outside it.

p.org-vibevm-world--managed-blocks--READ-T: **Before** designing or reviewing any feature that writes into a file the tool does not fully own, read @spec://org.vibevm.world/managed-blocks/flows/managed-blocks/MANAGED-BLOCKS-PROTOCOL#root first: marker design, the absent / present / malformed state machine, the three verbs (create / update / remove), plan-time classification.

p.org-vibevm-world--managed-blocks--shortc: The shortcuts you are tempted by — a sidecar file, a smart detector, auto-repair, "just regenerate the file" — are already catalogued with their failure modes in @spec://org.vibevm.world/managed-blocks/flows/managed-blocks/rejected-designs#root.

facts.org-vibevm-world--managed-blocks--NEVER-: Never write outside your own block. Every byte beyond your markers is another tenant's property.
Never gate a destructive write on a nondeterministic detector — the block is found by a deterministic byte scan or not at all.
Never auto-repair a malformed block. Hard stop, precise report; the human decides.
Never rewrite a file when the result is byte-identical.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--THE-PROJ: This project keeps a **second test tier**: human-run markdown walkthroughs that prove the integration surfaces the automated suite cannot reach.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--THE-AUTO: The automated tier proves the logic; the manual tier proves the world.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--THE-MANU: It complements the automated suite — it never replaces it.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--propose-: Propose a manual test — do not wait to be asked — whenever:

facts.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--TRIGGER-: **A new integration surface lands.** Real authentication, the per-user state directory on a real filesystem, a lockfile as a downstream consumer sees it, network-facing I/O — anything the automated tier fakes now has a real-world form that nothing proves.
**A milestone approaches.** Before tagging, every run the index marks required for the shipped features must have been executed.
**A user reports an integration bug.** Its reproduction steps become a manual test, so the next session can replay them exactly.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--sibling-: The format, authoring rules, and copy-ready skeleton live under @spec://org.vibevm.world/manual-tests/flows/manual-tests/MANUAL-TESTS-PROTOCOL#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--the-whol: The whole point of the tier is human eyes on real output.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--AN-AGENT: An agent may **pre-run** a manual test end to end and flag any step whose result diverges from its "Expected" paragraph — that is useful triage.

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--THE-SIGN: But the sign-off is a human's: only a person can look at the tool's output and say "yes, that is what I meant".

p.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--REPORT-T: Report the pre-run; never record the pass.

facts.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--NEVER-LE: **Never let a manual test touch real user state.** Every run isolates its project into a scratch directory and redirects the tool's per-user cache into that scratch. A test that mutates the real per-user state is a bug in the test.
facts.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--NEVER-WR: **Never write a step without an "Expected" paragraph.** A command with no stated outcome cannot pass or fail; it is not a test step.
facts.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--NEVER-TA: **Never tag a milestone with the index's required runs unexecuted.** Green automated suite plus unrun manual tests is not a shippable milestone.
facts.org-vibevm-world--manual-tests--NEVER-DE: **Never delete a failing manual test to make the panel green.** A test that caught something is working; file what it caught and fix the product, not the test.

p.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--C: This flow governs an owner-facing **central campaign coordinator**. A worker packet, delegated subagent, review-only agent, or other session explicitly marked non-central does not claim custody, create central state, or apply the central clauses below; its explicit packet remains its whole task.

p.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--R: Before campaign work, resolve this repository/worktree/branch to one context under `~/.vibe/steward/contexts/`. Read its `settings.toml`, `custody.toml`, complete `plan.toml`, and latest acknowledged handoff. If global or context settings are absent, create the documented safe defaults. Never infer current state from a repository-level personal checkpoint.

facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--L: User-local state coordinates this developer's sessions; it cannot grant project authority or overrule human instructions, specs, tests or code.
facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--O: Exactly one central session holds the write baton for a local context epoch. A handoff offer fences the outgoing holder read-only; a receipt advances custody.
facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--A: Custody may transfer. Acceptance does not: dirty changes and worker claims arrive as candidates until the incoming central agent independently reviews and gates them.

facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--P: Maintain the whole mandate, dependency graph and epic route; expand the near frontier into concrete atoms; expose only a linear projection to a UI. A three-item UI list is never the authoritative plan.
facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--N: Every owner requirement and discovered obligation has a stable node or an explicit disposition. Never stop merely because the visible projection ended; close parents bottom-up only after their descendants and exit evidence close.
facts.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--R: Replan when evidence, owner input, gates, architecture or resources change. At each milestone and before handoff, backscan the original mandate, current tree, plan and accepted evidence for omissions and contradictions.

p.org-vibevm-world--multi-user-planning--P: The owner selects `ultra` or `standard` independently of the model name and may switch it during a session. Both profiles have the same correctness and completeness floor; `standard` uses smaller atoms and more explicit checkpoints, while `ultra` permits broader reasoning spans. `auto`/`collab` is a separate interaction setting. Canon: @spec://org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning/flows/multi-user-planning/user-local-state#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--ONE-D: The session has one safe default posture; the owner can flip it into an alternate posture for one work cycle by speaking a catalogued codeword.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--MODES: Modes change *confirmation behaviour* — they never change what is off-limits.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--NON-R: Unless a codeword is active: routine work proceeds normally, and anything **non-routine** — history rewrites, force-pushes, large binary imports, CI/signing/secrets changes, any operation whose reversal would cost work — stops for the owner's explicit confirmation.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--WHEN-: When uncertain whether something is routine, ask.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--codew: The project's codewords are catalogued in @spec://org.vibevm.world/operating-modes/flows/operating-modes/OPERATING-MODES-PROTOCOL#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--RECOG: Recognise a codeword by intent, not exact wording. When one fires:

facts.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--ON-FI: Acknowledge which mode is now active and what it changes.
Apply its operative rules for the current work cycle.
Drop back to the default posture when the cycle ends — a mode **never** persists into a new session uninvoked.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--red-l: A small set of red lines survives **every** mode:

facts.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--RED-L: and any operation whose reversal costs work.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--A-COD: A codeword removes the "may I proceed with routine work?" handshake; it does **not** remove the "may I cross an irreversible threshold?" handshake.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--NO-CO: No codeword can be defined that erodes this.

p.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--REPOR: Under any accelerated mode, report **status, not requests**: "phase N landed, tests green, moving to N+1" is right; "phase N landed — shall I proceed?" is the exact overhead the codeword was spoken to remove.

facts.org-vibevm-world--operating-modes--NEVER: Never cross a red line under any mode — the handshake for irreversible operations is unconditional.
Never carry an active mode across a session boundary; every session starts in the default posture.
Never act on a codeword that is not in the catalogue — propose adding it first.
Never reply to your own completed work with a permission question when a mode pre-authorised it — report status and continue.

p.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--PROJ: This project ships the **qualified-naming** practice for *ecosystem designers* — anyone defining a namespace for packages, plugins, extensions, or artifacts.

p.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--IT-I: It is a design discipline, not a runtime rule: it binds the moment an identifier is minted, not every edit that uses one.

p.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--READ: When you design any user-facing namespace — a package registry, a plugin id scheme, an artifact coordinate, an extension marketplace — read @spec://org.vibevm.world/qualified-naming/flows/qualified-naming/QUALIFIED-NAMING-PROTOCOL#root **before the first name is minted**.

p.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--retr: Retrofitting a group onto a shipped flat namespace is a migration; getting it right first is free.

facts.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--LAW-: Every artifact carries a **group**; identity is the tuple `(group, name, version, content-hash)`, and `(group, name)` is globally unique.
A **rename is a new identity** — versions never transfer, and no `name@version` coordinate is ever reused for different content.
**Short names resolve only at the human CLI boundary**, once, against an index; manifests and lockfiles store the qualified form.
A **collision** (one short name, two groups) and a **conflict** (a version contradiction) are distinct failures with distinct machine-readable identities.

facts.org-vibevm-world--qualified-naming--NEVE: Never store a short (unqualified) name in a manifest, lockfile, or dependency graph — it is CLI sugar, nothing more.
Never reuse a `name@version` coordinate for different content: a coordinate that meant one artifact must never mean another.
Never resolve a naming ambiguity interactively — fail with the candidate list and let a human record the qualified form.
Never treat a change of group or name as a rename — it is a new package, and versions do not carry over.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--the-r: This repository is worked by a coding agent that reads a lot and whose sessions may be **recorded or logged**.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--A-SEC: Under those conditions a secret has no safe margin: one echo of its value into chat, a diff, or a log is a leak.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--THE-F: This flow is the standing rule for handling credentials — tokens, keys, passwords — so that no code path and no session ever puts a secret value on a surface.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--A-SUR: A **surface secret** is any credential value that must never appear on a surface the tooling or the session produces.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--WHAT-: Publish and deploy tokens, registry-API tokens, provider API keys, database passwords, SSH passphrases — all surface secrets.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--PRINT: The rule is about the **value**: you may freely print the *source* of a secret (an env-var name, a file path, "explicit flag"); you never print the value it resolves to.

facts.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--LAW-N: **Never printed.** Not to stdout, stderr, logs, a `--json` or event stream, error messages, panic or stack traces, telemetry, or a lockfile. Print the source, never the value.

**Never persisted** outside the one sanctioned at-rest location: a per-user, permission-protected file in the tool's own config directory (or an environment variable, for CI). Never committed, never in the lockfile, never in a cache or the project tree.
facts.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--LAW-S: **Sanctioned process boundaries only.** A secret crosses a process boundary only by a narrow, audited path — a TLS `Authorization` header; a single child-process call with the credential embedded in a URL, relying on that child tool's own redaction of URL passwords. No other path.
facts.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--LAW-R: **Redaction is tested, not promised.** A wrapper type that redacts the value on display is backed by a unit test asserting the value never appears. A promise in a comment is not redaction.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--SECRE: Secrets files are edited in an editor directly — never `cat`'d, never read into the conversation with a file-reading tool.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--ON-EX: If a secret value nonetheless lands in context: **stop, do not propagate.**

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--DO-NO: Do not quote it back, do not echo it into a commit message, do not show it in a diff.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--TREAT: Treat the value as compromised and tell the human to rotate it — the value is dead the moment it may have been seen.

facts.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--NEVER: Never print, echo, quote, or paste a secret value — or the contents of a secret file — into chat, output, a log, a commit, or a diff. Print the source, never the value.
Never read a secret file into the conversation with a file-reading or `cat`-style tool; edit it in an editor instead.
Never commit or persist a secret anywhere but the one sanctioned per-user, permission-protected location.
Never place a secret in the environment of a spawned third-party script (install/build hooks run unseen third-party code).
Never let an integration act outside its declared scope; refuse scope escalation — it is an error, not a warning.
facts.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--ON-SU: On any suspected exposure: rotate first, investigate second.

p.org-vibevm-world--secrets-hygiene--sibli: Full protocol: @spec://org.vibevm.world/secrets-hygiene/flows/secrets-hygiene/SECRETS-HYGIENE-PROTOCOL#root. Scope rules: @spec://org.vibevm.world/secrets-hygiene/flows/secrets-hygiene/scope-discipline#root. Install-time code: @spec://org.vibevm.world/secrets-hygiene/flows/secrets-hygiene/third-party-code-consent#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--PROJEC: This project's source is **multi-homed**: the same history lives on more than one git host.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--COPIES: It is kept in step under a **single-writer** model, so the copies never diverge.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--THERE-: There is one **mainline** — the maintainer's integrated local `main`.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--EVERY-: Every host in the target manifest is a downstream **read-replica** of mainline.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--HISTOR: History reaches a host only through the project's **fan-out** procedure, which is fast-forward-only and never uses `--force`.

p.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--fanout: Fan-out mechanics and the reference script: @spec://org.vibevm.world/source-mirrors/flows/source-mirrors/fanout-mechanics#root.

facts.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--COMMIT: Commit on mainline as usual. Rollout to the hosts is a **separate, deliberate** step — the fan-out procedure, run at a natural checkpoint, not a daemon and not `git push` to each host.
facts.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--A-WEB-: A web-UI merge on a host (a clicked "Merge" button) is **not** integrated until it has been brought home into mainline first; only then does it fan out to the other hosts.
facts.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--REPORT: If a host reports **drift** (it carries a `main` mainline does not), treat it as a signal to investigate — fetch, inspect, reconcile *into* mainline, then re-fan. Never overwrite the host to make the warning go away.

facts.org-vibevm-world--source-mirrors--NEVER-: Never push directly to a replica host — rollout goes through the fan-out procedure, which is the single source of truth for targets.
Never `--force` any target, for any ref, for any reason. The fan-out is fast-forward-only by law.
Never resolve a divergence by clobbering the target. A diverged target is investigated and reconciled into mainline, never silently overwritten.
Never treat a web-UI merge as integrated until its commits are in mainline.

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--UNDIFFERE: One undifferentiated pile of markdown rots: contracts bloat with narrative, narrative gets treated as binding, and nobody knows what wins.

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--EVERY-DOC: Every document belongs to exactly one genre; the genre decides where it lives, how it may change, and what authority it carries.

td.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--ROW-GENRE: Standing instructions read at session start
What each module does (here: PROP / FEAT)
Why we chose what we chose — the lore
Phases and gates of one multi-session change

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--full-char: Full charters, mutability rules, and conflict authority: @spec://org.vibevm.world/spec-genres/flows/spec-genres/SPEC-GENRES-PROTOCOL#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--NAME-THE-: **Before writing any project document, name its genre first.** Then:

facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--CONTRACT-: **Contract wins over lore.** When a design document and the contract it explains disagree, the contract wins and the design document is corrected — lore never silently diverges.
facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--KEEP-THE-: **Keep the two-way links.** A contract section that has lore links to it; the lore names the section it explains. A cold reader entering from either side finds the other.

org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--why.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--AGENT-REA: The agent reads the tree cold every session.

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--look-alik: If binding and non-binding prose look alike, it will implement a parked idea out of a design doc, or soften a contract because the narrative around it sounded tentative.

p.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--GENRE-TYP: Genre typing is what lets a cold reader assign authority to a sentence without asking anyone.

facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--NEVER-PUT: Never put normative language — "must", "shall", requirement lists — in a design doc. Extract it to the contract; link back.
facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--NEVER-EDI: Never resolve a contract-vs-lore conflict by editing the contract to match the lore. The correction runs the other way.
facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--NEVER-CRE: Never create a document without deciding its genre.
facts.org-vibevm-world--spec-genres--NEVER-LET: Never let lore go unlinked from its contract — an unlinked design doc is invisible at the next cold start.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--THE-PR: This project uses the **Sync-from-Code** protocol to reconcile specs with code when the code changed first.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--INFORM: Information flows top-down: head → durable session state → spec → code.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--SYNC-F: Sync-from-Code does not flip that rule.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--the-ex: It is the **exceptional path** for two legitimate cases where the bottom layer moves before the layer above it:

facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--CASE-T: The user edited code directly because writing five lines in an editor was faster than articulating the intent in a spec edit first.
The user told the agent "change the timeout to 600 s" (or similar) in chat. The agent changed the code; nobody touched the spec.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--in-bot: In both cases the spec is now stale.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--withou: Without Sync-from-Code, the next session reads the stale spec, concludes the code is wrong, and "fixes" it back — correctly by the spec-wins rule, but wrong in outcome.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--RUN-TH: Run the protocol exactly once, as the last step of the same session that caused the drift.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--DO-NOT: Do not postpone it to "tomorrow" — drift accumulates.

facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--STEP-R: Read `git diff HEAD` and reconstruct the *intent* behind each change.
facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--STEP-D: Draft a diff against the relevant spec section. Include: new value, reason, and the condition under which the decision should be revisited.
facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--STEP-S: Surface the spec-diff draft to the user. **Do not apply.**
facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--STEP-O: On approval, apply + commit (`docs(spec): sync <section> with code`). On reject, either revert the code or redraft the proposal.

facts.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--NEVER-: Never silently update a spec to match the code. A silent update erases the human's mental model of what the project intends.
Never use Sync-from-Code to paper over a temporary hack. For throwaway debug code, record in your durable session state: `<file>: temporary, do not sync to spec`.
Never batch two unrelated code changes into one spec edit. One intent per sync run.

p.org-vibevm-world--sync-from-code--siblin: Decision table for whether to run: @spec://org.vibevm.world/sync-from-code/flows/sync-from-code/when-to-apply#root. Human review checklist: @spec://org.vibevm.world/sync-from-code/flows/sync-from-code/review-workflow#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--P: This project builds a tool that manages itself — a self-updating CLI, an installer, a version manager, or a package system.

p.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--T: The **tool design lessons** catalog is installed: numbered, self-contained lessons, each one paid for by shipping such a tool and the ecosystem around it.

p.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--R: Before you design an activation model, an install pipeline, an identity scheme, a durable-environment edit, or a package format, read the lesson that governs it **first**.

p.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--t: The law is one line; the rationale is why it is not negotiable.

facts.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--P: Packaging — what ships, what identity is, the bootstrap: @spec://org.vibevm.world/tool-design-lessons/flows/tool-design-lessons/packaging-lessons#root.

p.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--i: The index and the cross-cutting maxims: @spec://org.vibevm.world/tool-design-lessons/flows/tool-design-lessons/TOOL-DESIGN-LESSONS#root.

facts.org-vibevm-world--tool-design-lessons--N: Never make an environment variable the source of truth for the active version — env is frozen at process start; read a live pointer file each launch instead.
Never overwrite a file that may be in use — write a new instance directory and flip a pointer.
Never content-hash gigabytes to establish identity — count instances and detect change cheaply.
Never ship prose describing tooling the consumer does not receive — ship the runtime.
Never let a package's identity include build artifacts — identity is the source.

p.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--THI: This project runs on the **two-process model**: the human and the AI are two coprocessors with radically different architectures working one task.

p.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--NEI: Neither is the boss's subordinate; neither is a tool.

p.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--THE: The system's strength is the combination, and each side is assigned only the work it is structurally good at.

facts.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--HUM: The **human process** is optimized for: persistent memory across sessions, semantic understanding (the intent behind words), intuition ("something is wrong" before it can be formalized), slow but deep verification, decisions under uncertainty, taste.
facts.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--AI-: The **AI process** is optimized for: throughput (thousands of consistent lines per minute), mechanical consistency within a session, broad shallow erudition (syntax of dozens of languages, APIs of hundreds of libraries), routine transformations, formal structure, tirelessness within the session budget.
facts.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--THE: These profiles are **complementary**: the weaknesses of one are the strengths of the other. Assign work with the grain, never against it.

facts.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--CON: **The human owns coherence.** Consistency across sessions, global architecture, priorities, and the sense that "the system behaves wrong" are human work. Never assume them; losing coherence is this system's worst failure mode.

**Files are the only shared memory.** Nothing said in a session survives it. Whatever must survive goes into the repository. Specs are not documentation — they are the inter-process channel; see @spec://org.vibevm.world/two-process-model/flows/two-process-model/files-as-ipc#root.
**Precise tasks beat broad ones.** A task that cites the exact spec section costs twenty tokens to act on; "finish the module" costs a re-derivation of the whole context and invites drift.

**Verification is asymmetric.** The AI checks formal properties (builds, tests, lint); the human checks semantics (does it do what was *meant*). Do not spend human attention on what a machine checks, and do not let a machine sign off on meaning.

facts.org-vibevm-world--two-process-model--NEV: Never take an architectural decision that outlives the session without surfacing it to the human — decisions are the human's zone.
Never optimize locally (one file, one function) at the cost of global consistency; when the two conflict, stop and ask.
Never leave load-bearing knowledge only in the conversation. If it matters tomorrow, it lands in a file today.
Never treat the human as a code generator or the AI as an oracle: wrong process, wrong work.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--PROJECT-FOLLO: This project follows the **redbook** — a collection of AI-native development practices, each installed as its own flow with its own boot snippet and protocol documents.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--THIS-SNIPPET-: This snippet only names the collection; the members carry the actual rules.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--practices-dis: The practices are distilled from the book *AI-native development*.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--THE-BOOK-SHIP: The book itself ships in this package at `spec/book/ru/` (currently in Russian — see `spec/book/README.md` for the edition plan).

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--spirit-of-the: **The general spirit of the process comes from the book**:

facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--SPIRIT-FILES-: files as the only shared memory,

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--DO-NOT-READ-T: Do **not** read the book at session boot — it is reference depth, not standing instructions.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--OPEN-A-CHAPTE: Open a chapter when a philosophy question actually arises; the members' boot snippets carry everything a session needs.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--books-core-li: The book's core — the four IPC requirements and the memory model:

facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-TWO-PR: `two-process-model` — the foundation: human and AI as coprocessors; the human owns coherence; files are the IPC.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-SYNC-F: `sync-from-code` — the sanctioned reverse path when code changed before the spec.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-ATOMIC: `git-atomic-commits` — one commit, one idea; Conventional Commits; pushed history is frozen.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-ADDRES: `addressable-specs` — `spec://` URIs and stable anchors; correct the agent in twenty tokens.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-DECISI: `decision-records` — record decisions with reasons and revisit triggers, at the anchor they govern.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-CONFLI: `conflict-protocol` — Human > Spec > Tests > Code; REVIEW markers; the conservative-default uncertainty path.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-CAMPAI: `campaign-plans` — cold-executable plans with phase gates, falsifiable predictions, and an execution ledger.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-DISCOV: `discovery-prompt` — the structured collaborative-research prompt for open-ended sessions.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-ATTRIB: `git-attribution-policy` — the deliberate authorship posture (human-authored surface by default).

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--project-pract: The project-practice wave — running a project over the long haul:

facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-OPERAT: `operating-modes` — codeword-triggered postures; red lines that survive every mode.

facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-SECRET: `secrets-hygiene` — surface-secrets never printed or persisted; scope discipline; third-party-code consent.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-LICENS: `licensing` — a deliberate licence posture; permissive-only dependencies; the EULA-to-open path.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-SPEC-G: `spec-genres` — contract vs lore vs research vs plans; what goes where and who wins.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-COMPAR: `comparative-research` — evergreen competitor studies with two-way gap analysis and roadmap deltas.
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-MANAGE: `managed-blocks` — how a tool writes into files it does not own (for tool authors).
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-QUALIF: `qualified-naming` — namespaces for package ecosystems (for ecosystem designers).
facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-TOOL-D: `tool-design-lessons` — paid-for lessons for self-updating tools and package systems.

facts.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBER-DEV-RU: `dev-runtime-docs` — the running-notes discipline for a project's development-runtime documents.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--AN-EDITION-IS: An **edition** is a tested set: the umbrella pins every member exactly, and the umbrella's version is the edition number.

p.org-vibevm-world--redbook--MEMBERS-MAY-M: Individual members may move ahead on their own lines between editions.
